title: Unimodality of Gaussian (q-)binomial coefficients

problemStatement.formal: For all n and 0 \le k \le n, writing \binom{n}{k}_q = \sum_{i=0}^{k(n-k)} a_i q^i \in \mathbb{Z}[q] with a_i \ge 0, the coefficient sequence (a_0,\dots,a_{k(n-k)}) is unimodal: a_0 \le a_1 \le \cdots \le a_{\lfloor k(n-k)/2\rfloor} \ge \cdots \ge a_{k(n-k)} (and symmetric, a_i = a_{k(n-k)-i}).
problemStatement.plain: The Gaussian binomial coefficient is a polynomial in q whose non-negative integer coefficients sum to the ordinary binomial coefficient. For example the coefficients of the polynomial for (5 choose 2)_q are 1,1,2,2,2,1,1. Unimodality says the coefficients rise weakly to a single central peak and then fall, never dipping and recovering. The problem is to prove this rising-then-falling shape in Lean 4.
whyMatters: Unimodality is a genuinely deep result (Sylvester 1878); the clean proofs use the sl_2 / hard Lefschetz structure on the cohomology of the complex Grassmannian, so a formalization would give Mathlib a nontrivial unimodality theorem and a reusable template.

It connects the gallery's existing division-free q-binomial development to algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, and exercises Lean's currently-thin support for polynomial coefficient extraction and unimodality reasoning.

proven: Symmetry a_i = a_{k(n-k)-i} and \binom{n}{k}_q = \binom{n}{n-k}_q (gallery: combinations-formula-oq-03, qBinom_symm)
Non-negativity of the coefficients (Gauss; coefficients count subsets/lattice paths by area)
Sylvester's unimodality theorem (1878), via the sl_2-action on partitions in a k x (n-k) box
Hard Lefschetz for Grassmannians gives unimodality of the Betti numbers a_i
O'Hara's constructive combinatorial proof of unimodality (1990), the most formalization-friendly route
open: No Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Gaussian-binomial unimodality exists
Mathlib has no general Unimodal predicate for integer sequences, nor sl_2 / hard-Lefschetz infrastructure
The bridge from the recurrence-based qBinom to its explicit Polynomial-Z coefficient sequence is unformalized
knownResults.goal: Formalize unimodality of the coefficient sequence of \binom{n}{k}_q in Lean 4: realize it as a Polynomial Z with coefficients = area-enumeration, define a Unimodal predicate, and prove unimodality (ideally via O'Hara's combinatorial decomposition), with small-k (k=1,2) cases as first milestones.

insights: The Gaussian q-binomial [n,k]_q is a PALINDROMIC polynomial of degree k(n-k): coefficient sequence a_j = a_{k(n-k)-j}. Over a field this is the reciprocity identity [n,k]_q = q^{k(n-k)} times [n,k]_{q inverse} (q nonzero).
Palindromy is exactly the SYMMETRIC half of Sylvester (1878): the coefficient sequence is symmetric AND unimodal. Unimodality is the hard half (Proctor 1982 via sl_2) and remains OPEN.

KEY MECHANISM: expand the original [n+1,k+1]_q by the SECOND q-Pascal identity and the reflected [n+1,k+1]_{q inverse} by the FIRST q-Pascal identity; the two sides then agree TERM-BY-TERM after the induction hypothesis. Using the same Pascal on both sides does NOT give a termwise match.

Invertibility of q is essential (not cosmetic): the reflection uses q^{k+1} times (q inverse)^{k+1} = 1, so the natural home is a field with q nonzero. Over a general ring one would instead use a polynomial reversal.

Truncated natural-subtraction never bites: the delicate rewrite n-k = (n-k-1)+1 is used only in the branch k<n where n-k >= 1; the diagonal (k=n, both sides 1) and above-diagonal (k>n, both vanish) are dispatched first.

Working over ℤ[X] with q=X (rather than a field) is the right setting to talk about the coefficient ARRAY: nonnegativity needs an ordered ring; degree/monic follow from the X^{k+1}-shifted Pascal summand strictly dominating (n-k≥1).
Palindromy (existing) + pinned extremes (=1) + coefficient nonnegativity give the full symmetric-boundary structure; only the interior unimodality (Sylvester/Proctor) remains open.

Coefficient palindromy over ℤ[X] is cleanest via Polynomial.reflect (not reverse): reflect N is additive (reflect_add) and multiplicative on degree-matched factors (reflect_mul (f g)(natDegree f≤F)(natDegree g≤G): reflect(F+G)(f*g)=reflect F f*reflect G g). Key: reflect ((k+1)(n-k)) A where deg A=k(n-k)=D−(n-k) → write A=1*A, reflect_mul with reflect(n-k)1=X^{n-k} (reflect_monomial+revAt N 0=N) gives X^{n-k}*A; reflect (X^{k+1}*B) → reflect(k+1)(X^{k+1})=X^{revAt(k+1)(k+1)}=X^0=1 times reflect(deg B)B=B. The palindromy induction re-uses the field-proof mechanism: reflect(P1-expansion)=P2-expansion (qBinom_pascal vs qBinom_pascal'). coeff form via coeff_reflect+revAt_le (revAt N j=N−j for j≤N).

UNIMODALITY REDUCTION (researcher-1, 2026-07-19, VERIFIED 0-axiom [propext,Classical.choice,Quot.sound]): added the structural reduction that turns the OPEN half of Sylvester's theorem into a one-sided monotonicity statement. UnimodalCoeffs predicate on ℤ[X] (∃ peak m, weakly increasing to m then weakly decreasing). unimodalCoeffs_of_palindromic_of_monotone_left: for any nonneg palindromic P with no coeff above degree d, weak increase up to ⌊d/2⌋ ⟹ full two-sided unimodality (peak ⌈d/2⌉); decreasing half is the mirror of the increasing half via hpal, odd-d middle plateau a_{⌊d/2⌋}=a_{⌈d/2⌉} also from hpal. qBinom_X_unimodalCoeffs_of_monotone_left instantiates it via the already-proven qBinom_X_coeff_symm'/_coeff_nonneg/_natDegree — so ALL that remains of Sylvester unimodality for [n,k]_q is the single hmono hypothesis (coeffs increase to ⌊k(n-k)/2⌋). qBinom_X_unimodalCoeffs_zero (k=0 case) confirms the pipeline is non-vacuous. k=1 column DISCHARGES the reduction unconditionally: [n,1]_q = [n]_q = 1+q+...+q^{n-1} has a FLAT left half (all coeffs = 1 on [0,(n-1)/2]), so the hmono hypothesis of qBinom_X_unimodalCoeffs_of_monotone_left holds trivially. First NONTRIVIAL column proved unimodal (degree n-1), upgrading the vacuous k=0 sanity instance.
Explicit q-number coefficients: (qNumber X n).coeff j = if j<n then 1 else 0 (qNumber_X_coeff), induction on [n+1]_X = 1 + X*[n]_X via coeff_X_mul.

Corollaries: qBinom_X_coeff_symm (coeff j = coeff (revAt (k(n-k)) j) via coeff_reflect) and qBinom_X_coeff_symm' (coeff j = coeff (k(n-k)-j) for j≤k(n-k), the a_j=a_{D-j} symmetric array of Sylvester).
